# Incident Report — Malware Infection, 2025-01-22

**Evidence:** `2025-01-22-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (39,427 frames, 2025-01-22 23:44:56 – 2025-01-23 00:38:18 UTC+4). No Suricata/IDS artifacts were present in the evidence directory; findings below are derived directly from packet analysis with tshark.

## 1. Victim Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.1.17.215 |
| MAC address | 00:d0:b7:26:4a:74 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ |
| AD domain | BLUEMOONTUESDAY.COM (workgroup/NetBIOS name BLUEMOONTUESDAY) |
| Logged-in user | shutchenson (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString, realm BLUEMOONTUESDAY) |
| Domain controller | 10.1.17.2 (WIN-GSH54QLW48D.bluemoontuesday.com) |

## 2. Malware Family

**Attribution: behavioral, not signature-confirmed** (no IDS/AV alert artifacts were supplied with this evidence).

The infection chain and C2 check-in behavior are a strong TTP match for **Matanbuchus 3.0** (PowerShell-based loader), consistent with the "ClickFix" delivery pattern reported for this family in late 2024/early 2025:

- Fake-verification landing pages (`authenticatoor.org`, `appointedtimeagriculture.com`) precede execution of a Windows Script Component (`.sct`-style `<component><script language="VBScript">` dropper).
- The dropper launches hidden PowerShell, opens a decoy tab (`azure.microsoft.com`), and pulls a second-stage script via `IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString(...)`.
- The second stage computes the victim's `C:` volume serial number, converts it to a decimal bot ID, and loops forever `GET`-ing and `Invoke-Expression`-ing commands from the C2 at that ID's URL — an unusual, distinctive check-in mechanism.
- Operator commands over that channel report status strings verbatim as `status = success` / `script: RunRH, status: OK, message: PS process started`, and stage in TeamViewer for hands-on-keyboard access — all hallmarks reported for Matanbuchus 3.0's operator workflow.

## 3. Timeline

| Time (UTC+4) | Event |
|---|---|
| 23:45:36 | TLS connection, SNI `authenticatoor.org` (82.221.136.26) — fake CAPTCHA/verification (ClickFix) page |
| 23:45:49 | TLS connection, SNI `appointedtimeagriculture.com` (217.70.186.109) — compromised intermediate site |
| 23:45:56 | `GET http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872` — VBScript/HTA-style dropper fetched |
| 23:45:58 | `GET http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1` — stage-2 PowerShell loader fetched |
| 23:45:58 onward | Beacon loop starts: `GET http://5.252.153.241/1517096937` every ~5.2s (bot ID = C: volume serial in decimal) |
| 23:47:01–23:47:05 | `GET .../get-file/TeamViewer`, `/TV`, `/Teamviewer_Resource_fr`, `/pas.ps1` — TeamViewer components + duplicate loader staged |
| 23:47:05 | Check-in: `?k=message = startup shortcut created; status = success;` (persistence via Startup folder) |
| 23:59:38 / 00:25:09 / 00:27:54 | Check-ins: `?k=script: RunRH, status: OK, message: PS process started` (operator-issued script executions) |
| 00:38:18 | Last beacon observed; capture ends. 584 total beacon requests over the session — infection remained active for the full capture. |

## 4. Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control**
- `5.252.153.241:80` (HTTP) — primary C2 server, no DNS lookup observed (hardcoded IP)
- Beacon URI pattern: `GET /<decimal_C_volume_serial>` (observed as `/1517096937`)

**Malicious/suspicious domains**
- `authenticatoor.org` (82.221.136.26) — ClickFix fake-verification lure
- `appointedtimeagriculture.com` (217.70.186.109) — compromised intermediary/redirector

**Malicious URLs**
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872`
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1`
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/pas.ps1`
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/TeamViewer`
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/TV`
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/Teamviewer_Resource_fr`
- `http://5.252.153.241/1517096937` (and `?k=...` status check-in variants)

**Transferred files and SHA256 hashes**

| File | SHA256 | Role |
|---|---|---|
| 264872 | c74123dbccded43fda61651e102750b041d4c3af6fda88cd6436f9276653e103 | Initial dropper (VBScript component) |
| 29842.ps1 | b8ce40900788ea26b9e4c9af7efab533e8d39ed1370da09b93fcf72a16750ded | Stage-2 PowerShell C2 loader |
| pas.ps1 | a833f27c2bb4cad31344e70386c44b5c221f031d7cd2f2a6b8601919e790161e | Duplicate/second copy of C2 loader |
| TV | 3448da03808f24568e6181011f8521c0713ea6160efd05bff20c43b091ff59f7 | TeamViewer QuickSupport component |
| TeamViewer | 904280f20d697d876ab90a1b74c0f22a83b859e8b0519cb411fda26f1642f53e | TeamViewer executable (RMM for hands-on-keyboard access) |
| Teamviewer_Resource_fr | 9634ecaf469149379bba80a745f53d823948c41ce4e347860701cbdff6935192 | TeamViewer localization resource |

**Persistence:** Startup-folder shortcut created (confirmed by operator's own C2 check-in message).

## 5. Notes / Ruled Out

- `drsuapi`/Kerberos/LDAP traffic between 10.1.17.215 and DC 10.1.17.2 at 23:45:11 is standard AD client authentication (opnums 0/12/1 — bind/DRSCrackNames), not DCSync (which uses opnum 3, GetNCChanges); not treated as an IOC.
- A TLS session to 45.125.66.252:443 at 00:00:13 had no recoverable SNI/certificate data and no supporting DNS query in the capture; insufficient evidence to attribute it to this incident, so it is not listed as a confirmed IOC.
- No TeamViewer protocol traffic (TCP/UDP 5938) to the victim was observed after the TeamViewer files were staged, meaning the remote-access tool was downloaded/installed but an active operator session was not captured within this pcap's time window.
